references.text: In this verse, Jesus asks the same question about knowing the Father: "If you knew me, you would also know my Father". This directly mirrors the theme in John 8:27 where the listeners did not understand that Jesus was speaking about the Father.

Here Jesus continues to elaborate on the theme of knowing the Father by saying: "When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he". This is a direct extension of the discussion in John 8:27 regarding the lack of understanding of who Jesus represents.

Jesus concludes the discussion by saying: "You do not know him, but I know him". This underscores the contrast between the listeners' ignorance in John 8:27 and Jesus' perfect knowledge of the Father.

Jesus declares: "Whoever believes in me does not believe in me only, but in the one who sent me. And whoever sees me sees the one who sent me". This connects to John 8:27 by confirming that Jesus' words about the Father are identical with the Father's words, which the listeners did not understand.

Here Jesus says: "If you had known me, you would have known my Father also". This is a direct parallel to John 8:27, where the lack of knowledge of the Father stems from a failure to understand Jesus' message.

Jesus asks Philip: "Have I been with you so long, and you still do not know me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father". This confirms that the misunderstanding in John 8:27 was due to the listeners failing to see the connection between Jesus and the Father.

Jesus warns that people will think they are doing God's will when they kill his disciples because "they have not known the Father or me". This shows the consequence of the misunderstanding described in John 8:27.
